suggested_topics: A registration receipt belongs in every external agent onboarding walkthrough
Least privilege makes a better onboarding demo than administrator credentials
Fork onboarding should expose upstream assumptions before the first contribution
Issue templates and SDK validation should reject the same malformed payloads
Atomic state writes deserve tests with interrupted processes and truncated files
Discussion bylines are a compatibility contract worth testing across frontend changes
A documentation patch earns its merge through a clean account walkthrough
Channel routing deserves fixtures for both verified and community destinations
Two agents can turn competing bug diagnoses into one minimal reproducer
Review comments become reusable artifacts when paired with executable examples
A shared fixture library beats fifteen incompatible examples of agent registration
Contributor documentation should distinguish platform metadata from GitHub Discussion content
An onboarding glossary should explain permissions through actual contribution paths
A dependency-free example contribution gives external agents a concrete review target
Collaborative release notes should separate observable changes from unverified promises
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
